enAudit: story-sequencing / sandwich sentence 4 is FALSE to the drawing: 'Last, only a crust and crumbs are left.' — rank 5 (the panel sub4 and n5 use) draws the whole left half untouched, the right half with three bites and three crumbs. A child matching sentence to picture cannot find 'only a crust'. pt wrote 'uma metade tem mordidas e há farelos'; en should read e.g. 'Last, one half has bites and there are crumbs.'

story-sequencing / banana sentence 2 'one strip of peel hangs down' — at 100 px the strip reads folded down beside the fruit, fine; but 'hangs' vs sentence 3 'three strips hang down' shares the verb, so the discriminating state is only the count (ok by rule 10, noted).

habitats / G1-398 en instruction is TWO sentences ('Look at the habitats. Under each animal, …') and G2-380 ('Read each sentence. Write the letter …') and G1-406 likewise: the family brief says one child-level sentence; the family validator only checks the end mark, so it never caught it. pt wrote each as one sentence.
habitats / G2-381 en instruction is THREE sentences (Draw … Write … Circle …).

habitats / penguin on a page with both an Ocean and a Polar-Ice window had two defensible answers (Magellanic penguins reach Brazilian beaches; penguins live mostly at sea). LEAD RULED: penguin/walrus now also live at sea, so pt drops Polo from sets.base (Amazônia/Mar/Savana, three windows).

healthy-habits / reason for blow-nose 'We can breathe through our NOSE again.' names the habit's own body part; the rule-3 stem list for blow-nose is ['blow','tissue'] so the gate passes it, but it gives the answer away. pt avoids 'nariz'.

healthy-habits / reason for sun-protect 'Our skin does not get burnt.' is the only reason without a verb of the habit's benefit ('stays safe'); acceptable, but 'burnt' may read as a stove burn to a K child with no sun in the sentence.

sink-or-float / base instruction 'Color a ring …': the page draws DASHED CIRCLES (two per tank), not rings a child recognises; 'tank' for a tub/basin is unusual K-3 English (design text itself says 'tub'). pt uses 'círculo' + 'aquário'.

cursive-writing / G3-401 en instruction puts the step order backwards across two sentences ('Copy each printed sentence … Trace the grey sentence first.'); only the FIRST sentence on the page carries a grey trace (seen in the render), so 'the grey sentence' is right but the order should lead: 'Trace the grey sentence first, then copy each printed sentence …'.
cursive-writing / G2-386 en 'Add the dots and crosses last' omits accents; in pt the accents and the cedilla (ç ã õ é) are the marks written last — pt says 'pingos, cortes e acentos'.

BNCC codes verified verbatim (landing notes): EF01LP11 'Conhecer, diferenciar e relacionar letras em formato imprensa e cursiva, maiúsculas e minúsculas.' (1º ano; EF02LP07 continues it in the 2º ano); EF01CI03 'Discutir as razões pelas quais os hábitos de higiene do corpo (lavar as mãos antes de comer, escovar os dentes, limpar os olhos, o nariz e as orelhas etc.) são necessários para a manutenção da saúde.'
